[…] there exists a positive integer d and disjoint subsets E_0, …, E_{d−1} such that for all i = 0, …, d − 1 and all x ∈ E_i, we have 𝒫(x, E_j) = 1 where j = i + 1 (mod d). The smallest positive integer d satisfying the above is called the period of Φ. An aperiodic Markov chain is a chain with period d = 1. A set C ∈ 𝓔 is called petite, if there exists a non-negative sequence (a_n)_{n∈ℕ} with Σ_{n=1}^∞ a_n = 1 and a nontrivial positive measure ν on (E, 𝓔) such that Σ_{n=1}^∞ a_n𝒫ⁿ(x, A) ≥ ν(A), x ∈ C, A ∈ 𝓔.")
